newsitem.title: USA: Dow up 50 points, NYSE sets program trading curbs.
newsitem.headline: Dow up 50 points, NYSE sets program trading curbs.

text.p: U.S. blue chips pushed to session highs in mid-afternoon, triggering the New York Stock Exchange's program trading curbs.
The Dow industrials rose 53 points or 0.7 percent to 7029, prompting the NYSE to impose its index-arbitrage curbs at 1424 EDT/1824 GMT.

A far sharper rally continued to gain steam in the technology and small cap sectors. The Nasdaq Composite gained 23 points or 1.8 percent to 1293 and the Russell 2000 index of small cap stocks rose six points or 1.8 percent to 352.
Broad indicators remained positive, with breadth favoring advancing issues by a better than two to one margin on both the NYSE and Nasdaq.
